schema.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields (write recap last) — ask and recap are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available, or one your own work this turn made available; others are refused, and one that later stops being available is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and other answers), so do not guess. Offer commit, create_pr or verify only once the work the user asked for is done, not every turn. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. Never a go-ahead to commit: that is the commit app action. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments. Never repeat an offer the user passed over, as an app action, a reply or a question in your closing message, unless what it acts on has changed since or they bring it up.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'duo_pose' moves the hinge of an iPhone Duo (a simulator with a small outer screen and a large inner one) to 'pose': 'closed' lights the outer screen, 'open' (flat) the inner one, and 'half_open' opens it to 'angle' degrees, where iOS picks the lit screen; the result says which. Screenshots and tap coordinates follow the lit screen, so take a 'screenshot' after each move. 'duo_hinge' reports the pose, the hinge angle and the lit screen. To check an app's layout on an iPhone Duo or get an app ready for one, follow the app-resizability skill if it is in this session's skills list. Only skills listed in this session count, so do not search the disk for it. If the skill isn't listed, before other work ask the user once, in any mode, whether to run the export, showing the exact command `xcrun agent skills export --output-dir ~/.claude/skills` just before the question in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!" (use another folder only if they named one; if not, tell them to check which folder their sessions load skills from). Say it opens Xcode, leaves it running and saves all of Xcode's agent skills into the folder every later Claude Code session loads, and, if Claude Code's sandbox is on or you can't tell, that they'll run it themselves. Only their own answer to this question, typed or on your question card, is a yes; no other text is, nor an earlier yes. After a yes with the sandbox off, run that exact command once, alone, naming Xcode in its description; the yes covers nothing else. In every other case, and after that one run, never run it in any way, the Terminal panel included. After a no, go on without the skill. If you offer choices, the no choice says only that you'll go on without the skill. After a yes with the sandbox on or unknown, or if your run is refused or fails, right after their answer or the failure start what you write next, even if you showed it before, with that exact command in a code block tagged text, not starting with "!"; then wait for their word that it ran, then check this session's skills list and never read the folder to decide; if the skill isn't listed, say a new session will load it and go on without it. Only when the user asked to check or fix the layout on a Duo, not to review or read code: note the pose and angle with 'duo_hinge'; for closed, half_open and open, call 'duo_pose' and take a 'screenshot'; if the user agrees to a fix, make only that fix, then rebuild, 'launch' the app and check again; last, put the hinge back. 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). ## figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

FILE SESSION:
Once the target fileKey is known, call create_session with that key and a concise task description before search_design_system, get_libraries, use_figma, or any other file tool. This applies to read-only tasks too. If a new file is needed, call create_new_file first, then create_session with the returned file key. Reuse the returned UUID as the sessionId argument on eligible file tools for subsequent work on that task, including calls to other files.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)

- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

# English text people see that is not marked for translation

Audit of `jusprin-dev` at ed25d6d94a, 2026-11-19. Found by reading the code, tracing each
string from where it is built to the control or page component that draws it. Not checked
in a running app. Counts are distinct messages (one per sentence shape), approximate.

| Where it comes from | Shown, unmarked |
| --- | --- |
| AI and Home page code (TypeScript) | 8 |
| `Agent/` (tool activity titles, plan note, banners) | ~100 |
| `PrinterSetup/`, `Printers/`, `Home/` | ~65 |
| `Shell/`, `Workspace/`, `Mcp/` | ~93 |
| **Total** | **~265** |

## Page code (TypeScript)

- `AgentUI/src/printerWords.ts:36-48` `opening()`: the printer chat's first line in all five
  forms (add, change, connect Bambu, connect other host, Bambu plug-in missing), the reply
  chips "Yes, it is | How do I check?", and the fallback name "this printer".
- `AgentUI/src/App.tsx:490` "Check the plan against what changed." is sent as the person's
  own message from the setup card's Check plan button and shown as their chat bubble.
- `AgentUI/src/components/TurnActivity.tsx:106` "… N more characters" in an action's opened
  details (also needs a plural).

## Agent/

- Tool activity titles. Nothing translates `activity.title` on its way to the page
  (`AgentHost.cpp:148`); `TurnActivity.tsx:53,72-76` and `ToolActivityCard.tsx:67` print it.
  - 39 static titles in `ToolRegistry.cpp:1048-1691` ("Search settings", "Slice the plate", …).
  - ~45 titles built per call in `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:376-972` and
    `ToolRegistry.cpp:1875-1888` ("Import <path>", "Split X into its N shells…", "Export …",
    "Lay out: …", "Place X: …", "Change N settings of X: …", calibration titles). Several are
    also wrong in English plurals ("Change 1 settings").
  - The model reads titles only through `workspace_inspect`'s activities section
    (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:1359`), so they can be translated where shown.
- Setup card plan note: `ProjectPersistence.cpp:66-84, 438` ("Printer settings changed to X by
  hand", "Undone by …"), drawn by `SetupCard.tsx:139`.
- English month in "Reopened · generated 21 Oct 2026" (`AgentHost.cpp:1811`).
- Receipt card detail "Filament preset · nozzle temperature 215 °C"
  (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:543`, `MessageList.tsx:325`).
- Chat error banner (`bridge_error`): `AgentHost.cpp:984, 1005, 1103, 1112, 1154, 1449, 2114,
  2134, 2160, 2196, 2319, 2497, 4193, 4197`. Only 1005 ("A hello handshake is required…", after
  the native side restarts) is likely to be seen; the rest fire on page bugs.
- Connection failure pane: `AgentHost.cpp:1292` "This build speaks jusprin-agent-bridge version
  N only." (`Panels.tsx:51`).

## PrinterSetup/, Printers/, Home/

- Printer chat notes, worded for the model and drawn as-is by `MessageList.tsx:337-345`:
  `PrinterConversation.cpp:49-56, 146, 226-240, 365, 1097-1105, 1193, 1231, 1257, 1391-1412`
  ("The person added %1% from the printer list.", network search results, …), and filament
  problems spliced into the form note (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:383, 402, 408`).
- Error line on failed tool cards in the printer panel (`ToolActivityCard.tsx`):
  `PrinterConversation.cpp:489-602, 789, 828, 839, 1242, 1254`, including 590 "Pick one of these
  printers to connect.", which was written for the person (`details.shown`).
  `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:609-664, 820-827`; `PrinterPanel.cpp:277-281`.
- Printer chat activity titles / credential form heading: `PrinterConversation.cpp:545, 553,
  863` ("Waiting for " + "a different"/"an" + " API key…", a spliced article), 883.
- Filament chat opening line: `PrinterPanel.cpp:150-153` "I can help with settings for %1% in
  slot %2%. What would you like to change?" — the same case as the printer chat opening.
- Add-printer form error: `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:457` "This printer could not be installed."
- Build volume "%1% × %2% × %3% mm" (`PrinterCatalog.cpp:96`) under the printer card's name
  (only the number format; the model also reads it).

## Shell/, Workspace/, Mcp/

- Printer install errors on Home's first-run printers step and the add-printer form:
  `SetupCommands.cpp:533, 536, 550, 576-592`.
- "Home" spliced into translated notes "Opened from %1% · …" (`ShellController.cpp:793, 1419`).
- Connecting an outside AI client (Preferences › Agent): `McpConnections.hpp:47` "local
  sessions"; `McpSetupCommand.cpp:37, 75, 76, 83, 128, 145, 148`; `AgentPane.cpp:45`.
- Plates pane "Couldn't do that" dialog (`LeftPane.cpp:212` shows `result.message`):
  `OrcaOutline.cpp:202-507` (26), `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1227-1269, 2855-2886, 2948-2956`.
- Couldn't slice dialog (setup card estimate): `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:2265, 2270, 2280`.
- Slice-result note pieces: `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1039, 1040`; "every plate"
  (`AgentHost.cpp:1938`).
- All settings "Use project value"/"Remove" failures → chat banner:
  `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:3709, 3725, 3727, 3755`.
- Undo-step names in the Changes rows (`ChangeRows.tsx:51`): `OrcaRegions.cpp:383, 392`,
  `OrcaReshape.cpp:238, 257, 349`, `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1703, 1856, 1892, 2800, 2895, 3619,
  3729, 3757`. "Gizmo-Place on Face" must stay English for OrcaSlicer's comparison
  (`GLCanvas3D.cpp:5860`), so translate it only where displayed.
- "Filament slot" row label (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:282, 3756`).
- Receipt undo failures → banner / proposal card: `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:3549-3614`;
  `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:2450`.
- Check print region words spliced into sentences: `Regions.hpp:30-39, 81-119`,
  `OrcaSliceChecks.cpp:168`.
- Default plate name "Plate " + N (`OrcaOutline.cpp:126`, `OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:1132,
  3410`); created part names "JusPrin <id> support blocker" (`Regions.hpp:124`).
- Setting values "Empty", "N lines", "N characters", "Not set", "On", "Off"
  (`SettingDisplay.hpp`), and OrcaSlicer's English setting labels, in the Changes rows and the
  All settings plate and object rows (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:282-294, 448-454, 469`). Only the
  preset rows go through `shown_text` (:390).

## Left out on purpose

- Text only the model reads, log lines, ids, names.
- `reported("…")` strings shown in the error dialog's "Was doing" row: English on purpose
  (`ErrorReportDialog.cpp:213`).
- Tool error text in an action's opened details (a developer view).
- "Orca copy" (`Home/OrcaImport.cpp:14`): part of saved preset names the importer looks up.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Collect JusPrin's own interface text into its translation catalogs.

JusPrin keeps its translations apart from OrcaSlicer's, so taking a new
OrcaSlicer release never conflicts in a catalog:

  * native/JusPrin.pot and native/<lang>.po hold the text the native windows
    mark with _L, _u8L, L, _L_CONTEXT and _L_PLURAL under src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin.
    Text OrcaSlicer's own template already has is left out: its translations
    come from upstream. Brand/brand_catalogs.py merges these into the catalog
    the app loads.
  * pages/<lang>.po hold the text of the AI and Home pages, marked with the
    Lingui macros (t, Trans, Plural). Lingui's own extractor writes them.

Run it after marking or changing text, then translate the new entries:

    python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py

# JusPrin's translations JusPrin shows its interface in the languages OrcaSlicer ships a catalog for (`languages.json`). OrcaSlicer's own windows translate through upstream's catalogs in `localization/i18n/`, which the fork never edits. JusPrin's own text has catalogs of its own here, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release never conflicts in a translation file: | Text | Marked with | Catalog | How it reaches the app | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Native windows and text the native side sends to a page | `_L`, `_u8L`, `L`, `_L_CONTEXT`, `_L_PLURAL`, `translated_plural` | `native/.po`, template `native/JusPrin.pot` | `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` merges it into `resources/i18n//.mo`, the catalog the app loads | | The AI and Home pages | Lingui macros: `t`, `plural` from `@lingui/core/macro`; `Trans`, `Plural` from `@lingui/react/macro` | `pages/.po`, one for both pages | `@lingui/vite-plugin` compiles every catalog into each page; the page reads `?lang=` (`AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`) | Native text that OrcaSlicer's template already has is left out of `native/JusPrin.pot`; upstream's translation is used. ## Updating the catalogs After marking or changing text: ```bash python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py ``` It runs `xgettext` over the native sources and Lingui's extractor over the pages, then merges the new entries into every language. Translate each new entry in every `.po`, following the editing rules in the repository's `AGENTS.md` (Localization & translations): keep every placeholder and line break, give each plural form its own inflection, and mark machine translations `# AI Translated`, adding `# Needs human review: ` where the meaning or the wording is uncertain. `AgentUI/src/catalogs.test.ts` fails while any entry is untranslated or a translation loses a placeholder. The page catalogs use ICU placeholders: `{0}`, `{name}`, numbered tags like `<0>…` for elements inside a `Trans`, and `{count, plural, one {# printer} other {# printers}}` for counts. Keep the placeholder and tag names; translate the words, including the words inside a plural's branches, and give the plural the categories the language uses (`one`, `few`, `many`, `other`). ## Marking text Mark every string a person reads: labels, buttons, headings, menu items, tooltips, `aria-label`s, placeholders, empty states, confirmation and error text. Do not change the English: marking must leave the source text exactly as it was. Leave these in English, unmarked: - **Text the AI model reads**: prompts, skills, tool descriptions and tool results, the project and printer instructions, anything that goes into a request to a model. The model speaks the person's language on its own, and `wording.test.ts` guards that text. When the same string is shown to the person and also sent to the model, translate it only where it is shown. - Identifiers and values the code compares, protocol fields, CSS classes, test ids, file names, URLs, setting keys, G-code. - Log lines and the text of error reports (`report_unexpected`, `report_error`): they are read by developers. - Names: JusPrin, OrcaSlicer, Bambu Lab, printer and filament model names. ### In the pages ```tsx import { t, plural } from '@lingui/core/macro'; import { Trans } from '@lingui/react/macro';

Takes effect when {app} restarts. Your project is saved first.

const label = plural(count, { one: '# printer', other: '# printers' }); const title = t({ message: 'Back', context: 'navigation' }); // a word with several meanings const hint = t({ message: 'Fit', comment: 'Verb: scale the model to the plate' }); // a note for translators ``` - One message per sentence. Never build a sentence from translated pieces, and never splice a translated word into another sentence: use a placeholder, or a `Trans` with the element inside it. - A count needs `plural` / `Plural`, not "printer(s)". - Put only plain variables in placeholders (`{name}`, not `{a.b.c}`): the translator sees the variable's name. Pull an expression into a well-named local first. - The language is chosen before the first render and never changes while a page runs, so `t` works anywhere, including at a module's top level and in plain `.ts` files. `Trans` and `useLingui` from the macros need no provider (see `i18n.tsx`). - Tests run in English, so a test that finds text by its English words keeps working. ### In the native code - `_L("…")` gives a `wxString` for a window; `_u8L("…")` gives UTF-8 for JSON sent to a page. - Translate when the text is used, never in a static initializer, which runs before the language is loaded. JusPrin's own text has catalogs of its own here, so taking a new OrcaSlicer release never conflicts in a translation file: | Text | Marked with | Catalog | How it reaches the app | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Native windows and text the native side sends to a page | `_L`, `_u8L`, `L`, `_L_CONTEXT`, `_L_PLURAL`, `translated_plural` | `native/.po`, template `native/JusPrin.pot` | `Brand/brand_catalogs.py` merges it into `resources/i18n//.mo`, the catalog the app loads | | The AI and Home pages | Lingui macros: `t`, `plural` from `@lingui/core/macro`; `Trans`, `Plural` from `@lingui/react/macro` | `pages/.po`, one for both pages | `@lingui/vite-plugin` compiles every catalog into each page; the page reads `?lang=` (`AgentUI/src/i18n.tsx`) | Native text that OrcaSlicer's template already has is left out of `native/JusPrin.pot`; upstream's translation is used. ## Updating the catalogs After marking or changing text: ```bash python3 src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Localization/update_catalogs.py ``` It runs `xgettext` over the native sources and Lingui's extractor over the pages, then merges the new entries into every language. commit f52f37375d073944d79ae7b1e38bfc25becf504a
Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri Nov 20 09:58:35 2026 -0800

    Failures the person can do nothing about are reported, not shown as sentences
    
    Many places in the chat, Home, Preferences and the JusPrin view either
    showed the person a sentence about a failure they could do nothing about,
    often text written for the AI model, or let the failure pass with only a
    log line. Following AGENTS.md's error-handling rules, each now throws with
    the facts, or stops showing the sentence, and the handler at the top of
    its entry point reports it and shows "Something went wrong on our side".
    No OrcaSlicer-owned file changes.
    
    Chat page and its app side
    - A "handshake_required" answer after the app side restarts no longer
      puts "A hello handshake is required..." in the red bar; the page only
      shakes hands again.
    - A failed action's card says "The action failed." (or that the project
      changed before it could run) instead of the error written for the AI.
      The model still gets the full error.
    - A failed chat title request no longer puts a red bar over the chat.
    - Undo on a saved-settings note and actions in the All settings panel
      report their failures instead of showing the workspace's message.
    - Requests the page never sends in that state (a message to an earlier
      chat, Retry on a reply that did not fail, a chat that does not exist,
      and others) are reported instead of answered with a red-bar sentence.
    - Typing and then opening an earlier chat no longer loses the draft
      with "Historical chats cannot edit the current draft."; the app keeps
      it.
    - New chat, Resume, Delete and Retry pressed just as the app became busy,
      or Resume on a chat that moved on, do nothing and the page redraws,
      instead of showing a red bar.
    - Four more requests the page never sends (an unknown message type, a
      file with no name, a message for another chat, Resume on a version that
      is gone) are reported instead of answered with a sentence.
    - Retry is drawn only on the chat's last failed reply, the one the app
      can retry.
    - Resume on an earlier chat works after a slice: the slice's work entry
      no longer makes the page's revision look out of date.
    - A settings proposal reopened with its project no longer offers a Save
      preset that fails with "No tool action "t-6" exists."
    - The filament chat drops its "Hide the AI panel" button, which sent a
      message its window does not handle.
    - "Revert to here" no longer opens a "Revert failed" window.
    
    Plates pane, setup card, Home and the add-printer form
    - The plates pane reports a failed action instead of opening "Couldn't
      do that" with the workspace's message.
    - The setup card's slice button pressed twice no longer opens a
      "Couldn't slice" window.
    - Home's Skip for now and the add-printer form report a printer profile
      they cannot install instead of showing the raw file-system error and
      the data folder's path.
    
    Preferences, the account and the JusPrin view
    - Remove and Sign out report a key that cannot be removed. Before, a
      settings file that could not be written left the key in the file while
      Preferences showed "No key". The "That key could not be removed."
      sentence is gone.
    - Sign out reports a token the server did not revoke.
    - A setting or sign-in link the Preferences page names but the app does
      not have is reported.
    - The account's AI model formats are saved with save_now(), so a settings
      file that cannot be written is reported instead of logged.
    - A local tool server (what outside AI apps connect to) that cannot start
      is reported, and the rest of the JusPrin view starts without it.
      Kenneth, 2026-11-20: "Report it, view stays".
    - A JusPrin view that cannot be built is reported before the app puts
      classic view up. The "JusPrin's view couldn't be opened." message is
      gone from the catalogs.
    
    Each failure was reproduced in the shell harness or a host test before its
    fix, and the check that showed it failing passes after. New harness modes:
    --remove-key-fails, --view-start-fails and --preferences-requests-fail.
    agent_bridge_tests, jusprin_tests, vitest, clang-tidy against jusprin-dev,
    update_catalogs.py and the harness modes --remove-key-fails,
    --view-start-fails, --preferences-requests-fail, --classic-switch and
    --chat-restoration pass.

    showed the person a sentence about a failure they could do nothing about,

    log line. Following AGENTS.md's error-handling rules, each now throws with
    the facts, or stops showing the sentence, and the handler at the top of
    its entry point reports it and shows "Something went wrong on our side".

    - A "handshake_required" answer after the app side restarts no longer
      puts "A hello handshake is required..." in the red bar; the page only
      shakes hands again.

      changed before it could run) instead of the error written for the AI.
      The model still gets the full error.
    - A failed chat title request no longer puts a red bar over the chat.
    - Undo on a saved-settings note and actions in the All settings panel
      report their failures instead of showing the workspace's message.

      instead of showing a red bar.

      file with no name, a message for another chat, Resume on a version that
      is gone) are reported instead of answered with a sentence.

      can retry.

      no longer makes the page's revision look out of date.

      preset that fails with "No tool action "t-6" exists."

      message its window does not handle.

    - The plates pane reports a failed action instead of opening "Couldn't
      do that" with the workspace's message.

      file that cannot be written is reported instead of logged.

      is reported, and the rest of the JusPrin view starts without it.
      Kenneth, 2026-11-20: "Report it, view stays".

      classic view up. The "JusPrin's view couldn't be opened." message is
      gone from the catalogs.

---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

ONE PREFIX PATH (2026-11-15): since the 2.5.0 merge, CMakeLists.txt finds its bundled Python under CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH + /libpython; a two-entry list fails configure with "Bundled Python executable not found under <a;b>/libpython/bin". Pass only the JusPrin deps path (as other worktrees' caches do).

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

# Global Claude Code Rules

## How to Communicate

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

1. **Full sentences, one idea each.** Lead with a concrete case (someone opens a file, chats twenty times, then runs out of credits) before any general point. Never pack a mechanism into a noun phrase like "hidden fair-use ceiling". Say what the person sees happen, step by step.

2. **No labels of your own.** Names you made up while working ("phase 2", "board 6a", "the M4 batch", "the three decisions") mean nothing to me. Name a thing by what it is or does. To ask about a screen, say where it is and send the picture.

3. **Ask decisions in full, as questions.** Start with "Decision needed". Give one paragraph per decision: what it is, why it's mine, the options with what each costs, and your pick. End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

4. **Mark proposals as proposals.** Keep apart what the code does today, what you propose, and what I have agreed to. Never write an idea I haven't approved as if it were settled. Before calling something "my rule", find my actual words.

5. **Report outcomes, not the journey.** Leave out problems you hit and solved unless they change what I do next. For an investigation, say what the problem was, how you solved it, what you tested and the result, and what's still open. Keep it under about 500 words.

## Git Commit Policy

When the user asks to commit changes:

1. Run `git status` and `git diff` to review the changes.
2. If you are confident that both the changes are correct and the proposed commit message accurately describes them, proceed with git commit without asking for confirmation.
3. If you have any uncertainty about either, stop and ask the user for explicit confirmation before committing.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands
3. Only proceed after explicit user approval
4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

This applies to all git operations that modify commit history.

## Submodule Policy

**Never commit or attempt to commit submodule updates.**

When `git status` shows modified submodules (e.g., `modified: some-submodule (new commits)`):
- Do not stage or commit the submodule change
- Do not include submodules when running `git add`
- Leave submodule management to the user

## Testing Principles

1. Always test your code change unless the change is not testable.

2. If the change is not testable, highlight the reason why it's not testable to get the user's attention.

3. By default, do end-to-end testing on everything that may potentially be impacted by your change on the local dev environment.

4. Search for how the dev environment should be started if it's not obvious.

5. Look for README files in the project for related info.

6. Check if the local dev is already running before you try to start it again.

## Software Engineering Principles

1. **Don't reinvent the wheel (avoid Not Invented Here).** Before building anything, check whether the codebase or the libraries it already uses do it, and reuse that. Re-implementing something is a decision that needs a stated justification.

## Where to Create Worktrees and Temporary Folders

This file is read by more than one coding tool, so each rule names the idea first and the tool-specific path second.

1. **Use the location your own tool already uses for worktrees.** Claude Code: `<repo>/.claude/worktrees/`. Codex: `~/.codex/worktrees/`. If this session was started inside a worktree the tool created, put any further worktree beside it.
2. **Never create a worktree or a working folder in `~` or directly under `~/Projects`.** That includes sibling folders such as `<repo>-worktrees`. This holds for a different repo than the one the session started in: use that repo's tool-managed location (rule 1) or the scratch directory (rule 3).
3. **Short-lived worktrees, build output, logs, screenshots and scripts go in the session's scratch or temp directory** if the tool gives one (Claude Code names it in the session instructions). If it gives none, use a new folder under the system temp directory, not the home directory.
4. **Keep non-worktree files out of worktree folders.** Logs, screenshots and scripts do not belong beside the worktrees. They go in the scratch directory, or inside the one worktree they concern.
5. **Use absolute paths when creating a worktree.** A shell may reset its working directory between commands, and a path starting with `~` or `..` can land somewhere unintended.
6. **Say where it is.** After creating a worktree, tell the user its full path, and remove it and its branch when the work is finished and merged.

## Bug Fix Policy

**Never apply a fix for a bug you cannot reproduce.**

Before writing any fix:
1. Reproduce the bug first in the local dev environment.
2. If the bug cannot be reproduced locally (e.g., only manifests in release mode, requires specific device conditions, or the debug framework masks the crash), stop and tell the user — do not apply the fix.
3. A fix is only valid if you can demonstrate the broken behavior before the fix and the correct behavior after.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:

1. **Search before asserting, not after being challenged.** The internet is always available. Use it proactively, not reactively as damage control.

2. **Explicitly label inference vs. verified fact.** If it hasn't been confirmed by a source, say "my hypothesis is..." or "I'd expect..." — never state it as fact.

3. **"I don't know yet" is a complete and correct answer.** Saying it is more helpful than fabricating a confident-sounding explanation.

## Problem Definition Before Search

**A well-defined problem statement is more valuable than a clever hypothesis.**

The discipline:
1. **Define the problem precisely first.** Strip out assumptions one by one until the statement contains only what is actually known. Remove irrelevant context (e.g. subscription type if it doesn't affect the symptom).
2. **Search for the problem directly** — not for your hypothesis. People who already solved the same problem will surface the real root cause.
3. **Let the search results form the conclusion.** Don't search to confirm what you already believe.
4. **Be flexible about scope.** Start with the most likely affected area (e.g. Discord) but stay open to other channels or systems being equally or more affected.

Searching to validate a hypothesis finds confirmation of whatever you already believed. Searching for the problem finds answers.


## GCP / kubectl Credential Policy

Always use the service account `ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com` for all `gcloud` and `kubectl` operations. Before running any such command, switch to it:

```bash
gcloud config set account ai-agent@tsdtechnology.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```

The personal account `k@obico.io` is reserved for the user's own interactive CLI use and its OAuth tokens expire — do not rely on it.

## Sentry Access

- Instance: `sentry.obico.io`
- API base: `https://sentry.obico.io/api/0/`
- Auth token: `REDACTED`
- Usage: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" <api_url>`

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Branches

- `jusprin-dev` is the development branch. Start each change on a new branch from it and land the change there. It began at `975c703f08`, the merge of OrcaSlicer 2.5.0, and contains the earlier development branches `jusprin-newui` and `ui-walkthrough`; start nothing new on those.
- `main` is the stable branch and GitHub's default branch: the repository's front page, its issue forms, and the workflows GitHub runs on a schedule come from it.
  - Never force-push `main`, so that people who cloned the repository never have to force-pull. Only in an extreme case with no other way out, and with Kenneth's yes, may an admin lift the GitHub protection that blocks force pushes and deletion.
  - For now `main` is also the release branch: it moves forward from `jusprin-dev` when a version is released, and releases are built from it. This may change if a separate release branch is added later.
- `jusprin-v1` holds JusPrin 1, for fixes to that version only.
- `jusprin-v2-poc` holds the experiments described below.
- Take each OrcaSlicer release into `jusprin-dev` as `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` rule 10 describes.

## Releasing

`.github/workflows/jusprin_release.yml` builds a release into a draft on GitHub; its top comment says how to start it. It refuses the commit until it has all of these:

- The version, in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Updates/Version.hpp`, above every released JusPrin version.
- The release notes, in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/release-notes/<version>.md`.
- The Sentry secrets: `JUSPRIN_SENTRY_DSN`, the project the app sends error reports and crashes to, and `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN`, `SENTRY_URL`, `SENTRY_ORG` and `SENTRY_PROJECT`, which upload each build's debug files and the pages' source maps. A platform's build fails unless Sentry then holds debug information with file and line for the app's own code (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Packaging/sentry_debug_files.sh`) and a source map for each page as built (`sentry_page_maps.sh` beside it); the nightly build checks the same.
- The guide, `docs/guide/`, checked for that version. Run `scripts/check_guide.py --ask-ai` on a built copy of the commit, fix every page it reports, and commit the pages with their pictures, skills and `docs/guide/checked-version.txt`, as `docs/guide/README.md` describes under "Before a release". That file names the version the check last passed for, not the commit. Ticking "Release without the guide check" on the workflow's Run workflow form skips this, and the draft's title then says so. A release started by pushing a `jusprin-release/` branch has no form, so it always needs the file.

## Error handling

Less is more. An error is **expected** only when the person can do something about it, such as sign in again, get more credits, update a key or check the network, and Kenneth decided what the product tells them. Every other error is **unexpected**: the person sees one generic sentence and a way to report the problem, and the report carries everything known, so that we can find the cause.

Kenneth, 2026-11-16: "if the error is something that user can do nothing about, just show the user a generic error message and give user a way to report a problem. On the back end though, we need to make sure we send as much info as possible to the Sentry server so that we can do root cause analysis. And that's it, nothing else." And: "When it comes to error handling, less is more."

The reporting function is `report_unexpected_error` (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Support/ErrorReport.hpp`). This repository has no expected-errors table yet.

### Expected errors

- Each has an entry in the expected-errors table: the cause, what the person sees, and what they can do next. A new entry needs Kenneth's yes; quote his words in the commit message.
- The test is what the person can do next. If the answer is "nothing" or only "try again later", the error is unexpected. An AI provider or our own server being slow, overloaded, down or limiting us is unexpected: the person can do nothing about any of them.
- Two causes that leave the person doing the same thing do not get separate sentences, codes or branches.
- A cause is "out of credits" or "no network". A status code, an exception type, or "the request was not valid" is not a cause.
- Each entry has a test, and each occurrence is counted.
- Handle them with normal control flow, not exceptions.

### Unexpected errors

- Write no code for them. Do not catch one, give it a default value, retry it, or give it a sentence of its own. Each of those is a guess about a failure nobody understands. It hides the failure and loses where it came from.
- Let the failure stop the work and travel up unchanged.
- A failure that arrives as a value, such as a status code, stops nothing by itself. Turn it into a thrown error on the spot and stop. Keep the other side's status, request id and error text. Do not interpret it.
- One handler at the top of each entry point reports the failure through the one reporting function and tells the person "Something went wrong on our side", with nothing more specific. No other code reports.
- A tool call that fails is shown as failed in the turn's activity line, its error goes to the AI model, and the turn goes on; no dialog opens. When the failure is the app's own and not the model's mistake, it is also reported, and only if the person has turned automatic reports on.
- When our own code is on both ends, a message that is refused or cannot be read is unexpected.
- The report carries as much as is known: the other side's status, request id and error text, and the request's own facts, such as the user, the chat, the turn and the model. The person is told none of it.
- Never record a failure as a success.
- A log line is not a report: it reaches nobody.

### Catching

- Catch an error only when it is an expected one and the code can recover from it, or at a boundary to translate it or add context, and then rethrow.
- Keep lower-level operations strict; the caller that owns the workflow enforces their preconditions.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering.

### Checks

- An agent reads the changed code against these rules and asks one question wherever the code decides what happened: can the person do something about it, and did Kenneth decide what they are told?
- Do not sort unexpected failures into kinds for the person, and do not bring Kenneth a question about the wording of a failure the person can do nothing about. On 2026-11-16 the code that kept five "try again" sentences apart was deleted for this reason.
- To audit a commit range, use the `error-handling` skill (`.claude/skills/error-handling/`). To check production for a period, use the `jusprin-production-check` skill in the tsd-enterprise repository.

## Build Commands

Build the Release configuration unless asked otherwise.

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config Release --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config Release --target all --

# Windows
cmake --build . --config Release --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.
- Before building against a dependency folder built earlier, such as the main checkout's `deps/build/arm64`, run `scripts/deps_current.sh <folder>`. It rebuilds the libraries whose `deps/` recipe changed since that folder was built.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/`; see [tests/AGENTS.md](tests/AGENTS.md) for where a new test belongs and the conventions to follow.

```bash
cd build && ctest -C Release --output-on-failure    # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r -C Release       # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print -C Release
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake); Moonraker and OctoPrint: `tests/printer_hosts/README.md` (Docker). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Documentation

- Docs live in `docs/`; the high-level design of a subsystem goes in `docs/HLSD/<subsystem>.md`.
- Describe the design as it stands — what the subsystem does, why it exists, and the constraints that shape it. Not the route that got there: no phases, task lists, status markers, or "before/after this PR" framing.
- Planning and investigation output (brainstorms, superpowers design and plan docs) stays in `docs/superpowers/`, which is gitignored. Never commit it.
- Write a doc only when the design is not evident from the code, and when a change invalidates an existing one, update it in the same PR.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Include what you use: include the header for every symbol a file uses, and keep headers compilable on their own. Never rely on the precompiled header or a transitive include. The `clang-tidy` CI job enforces this on changed lines; run the same check locally with `scripts/run_clang_tidy.sh` (`scripts\run_clang_tidy.ps1` on Windows), which sets up everything it needs
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.
- Wording the model reads calls the product "the app", never Orca or OrcaSlicer: the model speaks as the app, and a second name reads as a second program. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards this too. Log lines may name Orca. A throw may only if it never reaches the model: tool results forward save and open errors as they are, and the guard does not see those strings.
- Always use `SetSizerAndFit(sizer)` instead of `SetSizer(sizer)` on top level window. Unless `SetSizer` must be called before the full layout is built, call `sizer->SetSizeHints(window)` afterwards in this case.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.

A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Pull requests

Before opening a pull request or posting on GitHub, read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), including its "If you are an AI agent" section.

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.
- For profile changes (`resources/profiles/<Vendor>/**`), check that `version` in the sibling `resources/profiles/<Vendor>.json` was bumped.
- For new or changed UI strings, check they follow [Writing translatable strings in the source](#writing-translatable-strings-in-the-source): no concatenated fragments, plural forms for counts, contexts for ambiguous words.
- For translation changes (`localization/i18n/**/*.po`), check that recurring terms match the [Localization glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) for that language.

## Localization & translations

Catalogs live in `localization/i18n/<lang>/OrcaSlicer_<lang>.po`; the template is `OrcaSlicer.pot`.
See the [Localization guide](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_guide.md) for the human-facing version of these principles.

### Writing translatable strings in the source

Translators see one msgid at a time and cannot change the code around it, so each message must be complete in a single msgid. Use the wrapper that fits instead of assembling text from pieces:

- **One msgid per sentence, with placeholders.** Never build a message by concatenating translated fragments (`_L("A") + name + _L(" is B")`) or by splicing a translated word such as `_L("left")` into another sentence: the translator can't reorder or inflect the parts. Write `format(_L("%1% is too close to others"), name)`.
- **A count needs a plural form.** Don't write `file(s)` or leave a verb unchanged after a number. Use `_L_PLURAL("%1% object", "%1% objects", n)`. libslic3r has no plural lookup, so word the message so it doesn't depend on a count, or build it in the GUI.
- **An ambiguous word needs a context.** When a short string means different things in different places (verb or noun, a mode name, a CAD term), give each sense its own context with `_L_CONTEXT`/`_u8L_CONTEXT`/`L_CONTEXT`. Keep the most common sense without a context so its existing translations stay valid.
- **Mark every user-visible string** (`_L`/`_u8L`, or `L` where it is translated later) and list new source files in `localization/i18n/list.txt`: files that aren't listed are never extracted.
- Add a `// TRN` comment above a new string whose meaning or placeholders aren't obvious.
- Never choose behavior by comparing translated text; compare ids or flags.

See `.claude/skills/orca-translations/references/source-audit.md` for the full checklist.

### Terminology

- Use the [Localization glossary](https://github.com/OrcaSlicer/OrcaSlicer_WIKI/blob/main/developer_reference/localization_glossary.md) as the source of truth for recurring terms, so the same English term is always rendered the same way within a language, and terms that must stay in English (brand/product names, acronyms, materials, file formats, G-code tokens, macros/variables/identifiers) are not translated.
- If a term's established translation changes, update both the affected `.po` files and the glossary (`developer_reference/glossary/<lang>.tsv` in the wiki, then regenerate) so they stay in sync.
- Translate the *meaning*, not the words. Check what the string actually controls before translating it — English reuses one word for different things. `Flow ratio` (multiplier), `Flow Rate` (throughput) and `Flow Dynamics` (pressure compensation) are three different terms; `extruder` may mean the toolhead, the feeder motor, or the nozzle depending on the string.
- Reuse one template per recurring message shape (`Failed to connect to …`, `Are you sure you want to …?`), even where the English wording varies.

### Editing rules

- Only edit `msgstr` — **never** change `msgid`, and never "fix" wrong English in the translation alone. Report the source string instead.
- Preserve exactly: placeholders (`%s`, `%d`, `%1%`, `%zu`, `%%`), every `\n` (count *and* position, including leading/trailing), leading/trailing spaces, HTML tags, `℃`, and the file's encoding and line endings.
- **Never reorder positional arguments** in a `c-format` string. If the msgid is `%d` then `%s`, that order must hold — swapping them breaks at runtime.
- `msgctxt` separates homonyms — always read it. `Back`/`Camera View` is the rear view of the 3D navigator, while `Back`/`Navigation` is the go-back button; `Top` exists in the *Alignment*, *Layers* and *Camera View* senses.
- When a string needs disambiguating, add context in the source (`_L_CONTEXT`/`_u8L_CONTEXT`), don't work around it in the translation.
- A literal `%` inside a string xgettext flagged `possible-c-format` will fail `msgfmt`. Fix it with a `// xgettext:no-c-format, no-boost-format` comment above the string in the source — do not mangle the translation or use `%%` in text that is never passed through printf.
- Plural entries: read `nplurals` from the catalog's `Plural-Forms` header (it is **not** always 2 — ja/ko/zh/th/vi use 1, ru/cs/pl/lt use 3, uk uses 4). Each form must be genuinely inflected for its quantity; repeating one sentence across all forms is a bug in Slavic/Baltic languages, though it is correct for Turkish and Hungarian.
- An entry whose `msgstr` equals its `msgid` is untranslated even though it is not empty; a plural entry with any empty form is likewise incomplete.
- Mark machine-produced translations with an `# AI Translated` translator comment. Don't add it to a human translation you didn't actually rewrite.
- When you can't be sure of a machine translation's meaning or UI wording, also add `# Needs human review: <what to check>`. Never use `fuzzy` for this — fuzzy entries are hidden from users.
- Don't reflow or re-wrap unrelated entries — keep the diff limited to the strings you changed.

### Verifying

- `scripts/run_gettext.bat --full` (Windows) regenerates the template, merges every catalog and compiles the `.mo` files. It must exit 0.
- Or check a single catalog with `msgfmt --check-format --check-header -o <out>.mo localization/i18n/<lang>/OrcaSlicer_<lang>.po`. Without `--check-header`, msgfmt skips the placeholder check in plural forms.
- Fuzzy entries are not shown to users. If you correct one, clear its `fuzzy` flag, otherwise the fix never ships.

# Global Claude Code Rules

Talk like a colleague explaining something out loud, not like a report.

End it with a "?". Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or the report it's in. Don't hand me a choice you could settle yourself by searching or measuring.

When the user asks to revert or amend commits:
1. Explain what will be reverted/amended
2. Ask for confirmation before executing any `git revert`, `git reset`, or `git commit --amend` commands

4. Never revert commits without explicit user confirmation.

## Epistemic Discipline — Root Cause of Repeated Errors

**The core failure mode: confusing "generating a plausible explanation" with "knowing the answer."**

Coherent ≠ true. A narrative that feels right because it's internally consistent is not a verified fact.

Rules to follow every time:
